item.title: Basel Movement Document Guide
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
← Back to Basel Knowledge Hub

Block 1

Notification Number

References the unique notification number from the approved Notification Document. This links the Movement Document to its parent consent and must match exactly — any discrepancy will trigger a customs hold at the point of export.

View guide →
Block 2

Serial/Total Number of Shipments

Records the sequential number of this shipment against the total consented — for example, shipment 3 of 12. Competent authorities use this to track cumulative quantities and verify the movement remains within approved limits.

View guide →
Block 3

Exporter – Notifier Information

Confirms the identity of the exporter initiating this specific shipment. Details must be identical to Block 1 of the Notification Document. Any name or address variation between the two documents is grounds for rejection at the border.

View guide →
Block 4

Importer – Consignee Information

Identifies the receiving facility for this shipment. Must match the consignee named in the original Notification Document exactly. Changes to the receiving facility require a formal amendment before the shipment departs.

View guide →
Block 5

Actual Quantity (Weight/Volume)

States the verified weight or volume of waste in this specific shipment. Unlike the Notification Document which records intended totals, this block captures the actual measured quantity confirmed at loading and must not exceed consented limits.

View guide →
Block 6

Actual Date of Shipment

Records the date the waste physically departed the exporter's facility. This date must fall within the valid consent period declared in the Notification Document. A shipment date outside the consent window constitutes an illegal transboundary movement.

View guide →
Block 7

Packaging & Handling

Confirms the packaging types used for this shipment and any special handling instructions applied at loading. Must align with the packaging codes declared in the Notification Document. Deviations require documentary justification and may require authority notification.

View guide →
Block 8 (a-c)

Carrier Signatures (Chain of Custody)

The most operationally critical block. Each carrier in the transport chain signs here upon taking physical custody of the waste. Signatures must be sequential and dated. A gap in the chain of custody is a Basel Convention violation and can void the financial guarantee.

View guide →
Block 9

Waste Generator-Producer

Identifies the original producer of the hazardous waste being shipped. Must be consistent with the Notification Document and supports the legal chain of accountability from waste origin through to final disposal or recovery at the destination facility.

View guide →
Block 10

Disposal/Recovery Facility

Names the licensed facility receiving and processing the waste. Must be the same facility named in the Notification Document consent. The facility's operating permit must remain valid through the date of actual receipt — expired permits invalidate the movement retroactively.

View guide →
Block 11

Disposal/Recovery Operation

States the Basel Annex IV D or R operation code describing how the waste will be treated. Must match the operation code consented in the Notification Document. A mismatch triggers enforcement action by the importing country competent authority.

View guide →
Block 12

Designation of Waste

Provides a plain-language description of the waste type accompanying this shipment. Customs and border authorities use this block for visual verification against physical consignment contents. Vague descriptions are a common cause of shipment delays at border crossings.

View guide →
Block 13

Physical Characteristics

Describes the physical state of the waste — solid, liquid, sludge, gaseous, or other — as loaded for this shipment. Physical state directly affects transport safety requirements and must be consistent with the packaging type declared in Block 7.

View guide →
Block 14

Waste Identification Codes

Lists the applicable Basel Annex codes, national waste codes, and UN hazard classifications for the waste in this shipment. Must be consistent with the Notification Document. Inconsistencies trigger formal queries from transit and importing country authorities.

View guide →
Block 15

Exporter's Declaration

The legally binding signature of the exporter certifying the accuracy of all information in the Movement Document at the time of shipment. An unsigned Block 15 renders the entire Movement Document invalid before the shipment has left the country.

View guide →
Block 16

Additional Information

A free-text field for supplementary information required by competent authorities — such as emergency contacts, insurance references, or special transit instructions. While optional in most jurisdictions, some countries mandate specific content here.

View guide →
Block 17

Importer Acceptance

Signed by the receiving facility upon physical arrival of the waste. Confirms the shipment was received, quantities match the Movement Document, and the facility accepts custody. Without a completed Block 17, the exporter retains legal responsibility for the waste.

View guide →
Block 18

Receipt at Facility (Gate Check)

Records the facility's formal gate check — the physical verification of the shipment upon entry. Documents date of arrival, quantity received, and condition of packaging. This block is the operational trigger for the disposal or recovery process to begin under the facility's permit.

View guide →
Block 19

Certification of Disposal/Recovery

The final and highest-stakes block. Signed by the receiving facility to certify that disposal or recovery has been completed as approved. Until this block is signed and returned to the exporter, the financial guarantee (bond) generally remains locked under Basel Article 6.

View guide →

wp:postmeta.wp:meta_value: Complete guide to the Basel Convention movement document. All 19 blocks explained with field requirements, examples, and common errors to avoid.

item.title: Block 1: Notification Number
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Block 1: Notification Number

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 1

Block 1 – Quick Reference

Notification Number

Records the approved Basel notification reference that legally authorizes the shipment.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B
Field Type
Authority-issued reference
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 1 Captures

Block 1 links the shipment to an approved consent package. Authorities, customs, carriers, and receiving facilities use this number to verify legal status.

If this number is wrong or inconsistent across documents, the movement can be held, rejected, or escalated as a compliance risk.

How to Complete Block 1

1
Use the exact notification number from the authority consent. Do not substitute internal shipment IDs.
2
Match formatting exactly. Keep punctuation, country codes, and year sequence unchanged.
3
Keep Block 1 consistent across all shipment documents. Movement document, transport papers, and internal logs should align.
4
Verify before dispatch. Confirm the number still matches the latest approved consent revision.
⚠️
Wrong Number = Broken Traceability

If Block 1 does not match the approved notification reference, the shipment can be delayed at customs or rejected during compliance review.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Using internal load ID in Block 1
Correct
Use authority-issued notification reference only
Wrong
Minor character changes in code format
Correct
Copy exact code from consent letter
Wrong
Updating one document but not others
Correct
Sync Block 1 across all shipment records

Frequently Asked Questions

Can one notification number cover multiple shipments?▼

Yes, if the consent explicitly authorizes multiple shipments and Block 2 sequence tracking is correctly maintained.

Can I amend Block 1 after dispatch?▼

Only through documented correction workflow with relevant parties. Changes should never conceal original entry history.

What is the fastest QA check for Block 1?▼

Compare the value in Block 1 against the latest consent PDF and one transport document before release.

Supporting Documents

  • Doc 19: Movement Document Template (Annex V-B) - OECD decision text and movement/operation code instructions.
  • Doc 18: Corresponding Notification Number Rules - Official Annex V-A/V-B forms and completion instructions.
💡
DexMetal Expert Tip

Create a one-click copy source for the authority-issued notification number in your shipment checklist to reduce transcription errors.

← Back toBasel Movement GuideNext →Block 2: Serial/Total Number of Shipments

item.title: Movement Block 8: Carrier Signatures
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Block 8: Carrier Signatures (Chain of Custody)

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 8

Block 8 – Quick Reference

Carrier Signatures (Chain of Custody)

Captures carrier handoff signatures that prove uninterrupted legal custody.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B
Field Type
Custody transfer signatures
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 8 Captures

Block 8 documents who held the waste at each transfer point and when liability moved.

A missing signature creates custody gaps and compliance exposure.

How to Complete Block 8

1
List carriers in exact movement order.
2
Capture signature, date, and identifier at each handoff.
3
Confirm each carrier is authorized in approval records.
4
Retain clear evidence for intermediary transfers.
⚠️
Missing Signature = Broken Custody Chain

Custody gaps can keep liability with exporter and trigger enforcement risk.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Missing intermediary carrier signature.
Correct
Capture every transfer signature without gaps.
Wrong
Undeclared subcontractor signing.
Correct
Use only approved carriers or amend approvals first.
Wrong
Incorrect handoff dates.
Correct
Use actual transfer date/time evidence.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can digital signatures be used?▼

Only where accepted and auditable for all authorities.

What if carrier changes at short notice?▼

Follow authority-approved variation process.

Do all three carrier slots always apply?▼

Use all applicable handoff fields; do not leave actual transfers undocumented.

Supporting Documents

  • Doc 4: Transporter License / Duties - Operational transport requirements for hazardous waste movement.
  • Doc 23: Bill of Lading (Carrier Handoff Data) - Government bill-of-lading template for logistics documentation.
💡
DexMetal Expert Tip

Validate this block against your approved notification package before dispatch to reduce avoidable authority queries and shipment delays.

← Back toBlock 7: Packaging and HandlingNext →Block 9: Waste Generator-Producer

Block 2: Serial/Total Number of Shipments

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 2

Block 2 – Quick Reference

Serial/Total Number of Shipments

Identifies where this movement sits within an approved shipment sequence.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B
Field Type
Shipment sequence tracking
Required For
Multi-shipment notifications

What Block 2 Captures

Block 2 records the current shipment serial number against the total authorized shipments under the same notification.

Correct sequence tracking preserves legal traceability and prevents duplicate or missing movement records.

How to Complete Block 2

1
Enter current shipment serial and total approved shipments (example: 2/6).
2
Confirm sequence aligns with prior submitted movements.
3
Record cancellations/voids in your tracker before assigning next serial.
4
Validate the sequence in all dispatch and customs-facing records.
⚠️
Sequence Errors Trigger Holds

Wrong or repeated serial numbering often causes authority queries and border delays.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Using 1/1 for every shipment.
Correct
Use true rolling serial/total values.
Wrong
Skipping serials without audit note.
Correct
Document skipped/cancelled serials with reason.
Wrong
Mismatch between movement form and internal tracker.
Correct
Synchronize all records before dispatch.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can one notification authorize many shipments?▼

Yes, when explicitly approved by competent authorities and tracked correctly.

What if one shipment is cancelled?▼

Keep audit evidence and continue numbering per authority guidance.

Should serial format match consent letter exactly?▼

Yes, keep the same structure and notation used in approved documents.

Wrong
Mismatch with approved notification record.

Align Block 3 with consent file exactly.

Can notifier and generator be the same company?▼

Yes, if legally true and consistently documented.

Can a broker be notifier?▼

Only if that broker has legal notifier standing.

Should contact person be named?▼

Actual Quantity (Weight/Volume)

Records actual shipped quantity used for compliance and reconciliation.

Annex V-B
Field Type
Measured shipment quantity
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 5 Captures

Block 5 captures measured quantity at dispatch and supports downstream reconciliation.

How to Complete Block 5

1
Record actual measured quantity with approved units.
2
Source values from verified weighbridge or certified measure.
3
Check that total remains within consented quantity envelope.
4
Keep same units across movement and transport papers.
⚠️
Quantity Variance Is a High-Risk Trigger

Unexplained quantity differences can delay acceptance and bond release workflows.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Estimating instead of measuring.
Correct
Use measured values with traceable source.
Wrong
Mixing units across documents.
Correct
Use one consistent unit convention.
Wrong
Exceeding approved shipment amount.
Correct
Adjust dispatch or seek authority guidance first.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can minor variance be acceptable?▼

Sometimes, but material variance requires documentation.

Should gross and net be both tracked?▼

Track according to your approved method and record source.

When should quantity be finalized?▼

At dispatch, using final measured values.

item.title: Block 10: Disposal/Recovery Facility
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Block 10: Disposal/Recovery Facility

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 10

Block 10 – Quick Reference

Disposal/Recovery Facility

Identifies the authorized facility that will receive and process the waste shipment.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B and ESM principles
Field Type
Destination facility identity
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 10 Captures

Block 10 establishes the legal identity of the receiving facility — the specific site authorized to accept and process the declared waste. Competent authorities use this block to confirm that the destination is a real, currently permitted facility before consenting to the movement.

The facility declared in Block 10 must:

  • Hold a valid permit covering the declared waste type
  • Be the actual physical site of disposal or recovery
  • Match exactly the facility named in the approved notification
  • Remain authorized at the time of each shipment — not just at the time of notification

Block 10 identifies where the waste is going. What happens to it at that facility is declared separately in Block 11.

What to Enter in Block 10

Tick the correct facility type first — either Disposal Facility or Recovery Facility. These are not interchangeable.

Then complete the following fields:

Registration Number

The facility's official environmental or waste management permit number issued by the competent authority of the country of import. Include this where it exists — omitting it is a common cause of authority queries.

Name

The exact legal name of the facility as it appears on its permit or authorization. Do not use trading names or abbreviations.

Address

Full address including country name. If the actual site of disposal or recovery differs from the facility's registered address (e.g., a head office vs. operational site), enter the registered address here and note the actual site in the "Actual site of disposal/recovery" sub-field below.

Actual site of disposal/recovery

Complete this sub-field if the physical processing location differs from the address above. Leave blank only if they are identical.

Contact person

Name of the individual responsible for the shipment at the facility.

Tel / Fax / Email

Include country code. These details must allow authorities to contact the facility directly at any time during transit.

⚠️
If the disposer or recoverer is also the importer (Block 4)

Write "Same as Block 4" — do not duplicate all the information.

How to Complete Block 10

1
Confirm the facility's permit is currently valid and covers the specific waste type being shipped.
2
Tick Disposal Facility or Recovery Facility — match exactly what was declared in the notification.
3
Enter the registration number, exact legal name, and full address.
4
If the operational site differs from the registered address, complete the "Actual site" sub-field.
5
Cross-reference all details against the approved notification Block 10. The movement document must match.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Using a trading name or abbreviation
Correct
Use the exact legal name on the facility permit
Wrong
Leaving registration number blank
Correct
Always include where one exists
Wrong
Facility address differs from notification
Correct
Movement document must match approved notification exactly
Wrong
Facility permit has expired since notification
Correct
Verify permit currency before each shipment — not just at notification stage
Wrong
Omitting "Actual site" when facility has multiple locations
Correct
Complete the sub-field whenever the processing site differs from the registered address

Frequently Asked Questions

Can the facility change after the notification is approved?▼

Only through a formal variation process managed by the competent authority. Routing waste to a different facility without approval is a critical compliance breach and can result in the shipment being returned or seized.

What if the facility is also the importer?▼

Write "Same as Block 4" in Block 10. You do not need to repeat all the contact details.

Should permit status be verified for every shipment under a general notification?▼

Yes. A general notification can cover multiple shipments over up to one year. The facility's permit must be valid at the time of each individual shipment, not just when the notification was submitted.

What is the difference between Block 10 and Block 11?▼

Block 10 identifies the facility — who and where. Block 11 declares the operation — what will be done to the waste. Both must be consistent with each other and with the approved notification. See Block 11: Operation Code for the R/D code requirements.

Supporting Documents

  • Basel Convention Annex IVA – Disposal Operations (R/D code reference)
  • Country-specific Prior Informed Consent (PIC) approval letters
  • Facility permit or licence from competent authority of destination country
  • Waste management contract between exporter and receiving facility

Expert Tip: Facility details in Block 10 must exactly match the facility named on the PIC approval and the waste management contract. Any mismatch — including abbreviated vs. full legal name — is grounds for rejection by customs authorities. Confirm the full legal name and address with the facility before completing the notification.

Synchronize narrative and code set.

Omitting key process qualifiers.
Correct
Add essential qualifiers for clarity.

Can trade names be used?▼

Only as secondary context to technical designation.

Should chemistry details be included?▼

Include as needed for unambiguous classification.

item.title: Customs (Movement Block 16)
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Block 16: Additional Information

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 16

Block 16 – Quick Reference

Additional Information

Free-use field for any person involved in the movement to record information required by national legislation or operational necessity.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B Block 16
Field Type
Free text — national/operational data
Required For
Where national legislation or operational requirements demand it

What Block 16 Captures

Block 16 is a free-use field available to any person involved in the movement — exporter, carrier, importer, or competent authority — to record information required by national legislation that does not fit elsewhere on the movement document.

Common uses include: container or vehicle identification numbers, port transfer reference codes, additional authority reference numbers, national tracking identifiers, or any supplementary data that a specific country's legislation requires to accompany the physical movement. There is no standardized content — what goes here is driven entirely by the requirements of the countries involved.

This block is not a customs office block. EU customs office details for the notification form are handled separately on the notification document (Annex V-A Block 16). On the movement document (Annex V-B), Block 16 is the general additional information field.

How to Complete Block 16

1
Check national requirements for each country involved. Review the importing, exporting, and any transit country's competent authority requirements for what must appear on the movement document beyond the standard blocks.
2
Record container or vehicle identifiers if required. For sea freight this typically means the container number and seal number. For road freight, the vehicle registration. Include these where port or border authorities require them on the movement document.
3
Add national tracking or permit reference numbers. Some countries require their own tracking reference to appear on the movement document alongside the notification number from Block 1. Enter those here.
4
Leave blank if no national requirements apply. Block 16 is not mandatory for all movements. If no country involved requires additional information on the movement document, this field may be left blank without issue.
5
Label each entry clearly. Where multiple pieces of information are entered, label each one so authorities can identify what each reference relates to — for example: Container: TCKU3953742 / Seal: ML4489921.
⚠️
This Is Not the Customs Offices Field

EU customs office codes belong on the notification document (Annex V-A), not the movement document. Movement Document Block 16 is a general additional information field. Do not use it to record customs office data — that information belongs on the notification form.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Entering EU customs office codes in movement document Block 16
Correct
EU customs office codes go on the notification document (Annex V-A Block 16), not here
Wrong
Leaving Block 16 blank when the importing country requires a national tracking reference on the movement document
Correct
Check each country's CA requirements and enter mandatory national references before dispatch
Wrong
Entering unlabelled reference numbers with no indication of what they relate to
Correct
Label every entry — e.g. Container: TCKU3953742 / National Ref: TT-ENV-2026-041
Wrong
Assuming Block 16 is always mandatory and padding it with unnecessary data
Correct
Only complete Block 16 where a specific national or operational requirement exists — leave blank otherwise

Frequently Asked Questions

Who can complete Block 16?▼

Any person involved in the movement — exporter, carrier, importer, or competent authority — may use Block 16 to enter information relevant to their role that is required by national legislation or operational necessity. It is not restricted to one party.

Is Block 16 the same on the notification form and the movement document?▼

No. They share the same block number but serve different purposes. On the notification document (Annex V-A), Block 16 is specifically for EU customs office codes. On the movement document (Annex V-B), Block 16 is a general additional information field for any party involved in the movement.

How do I find out what each country requires in Block 16?▼

Contact the competent authority of each country involved in the movement and ask specifically what information they require on the movement document beyond the standard blocks. The receiving facility and your freight forwarder will often know from prior shipments what each country expects.

Does Block 16 need to be completed before the shipment departs?▼

Where required, yes — any information that must accompany the shipment needs to be on the movement document before dispatch. Container numbers and seal numbers are typically added at the point of loading. National reference numbers should be confirmed with the relevant authority before the shipment departs.

Supporting Documents

  • vCOP8 Official Movement Document — Annex V-B Block 16 — Official Basel source confirming Block 16 as the additional information field on the movement document.
  • Basel Convention Competent Authority Directory — Contact details for competent authorities in all Basel member states to confirm national Block 16 requirements.
💡
DexMetal Expert Tip

For ULAB exports from T&T, ask your freight forwarder and the receiving facility what each country expects in Block 16 before your first shipment. Build a standing checklist for each trade lane — container number, seal number, and any national reference. This becomes standard operating procedure and eliminates last-minute scrambles at the port.

item.title: Movement Block 17: Importer Acceptance
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Block 17: Importer Acceptance

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 17

Block 17 – Quick Reference

Importer Acceptance

Records importer confirmation that shipment is accepted into the destination chain.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B
Field Type
Importer receipt acceptance
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 17 Captures

Block 17 marks importer-side acceptance and a key transfer in accountability workflow.

Acceptance should reflect actual received shipment condition and details.

How to Complete Block 17

1
Capture importer acceptance date and authorized signature.
2
Confirm receipt matches declared shipment details.
3
Record discrepancies immediately if any are found.
4
Share acceptance evidence with required parties.
⚠️
Late or Missing Acceptance Extends Liability

Without clear acceptance evidence, closure and accountability remain uncertain.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Pre-signing before physical receipt.
Correct
Sign only after verified receipt event.
Wrong
Ignoring mismatch at acceptance.
Correct
Record discrepancy and trigger corrective process.
Wrong
Missing importer authorization proof.
Correct
Use authorized receiving representative only.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does acceptance close exporter liability fully?▼

Not fully; final closure depends on later completion certification.

Can acceptance be conditional?▼

Yes, if clearly documented with discrepancy notes.

Should acceptance be sent to exporter immediately?▼

Yes, prompt sharing improves compliance tracking.

Supporting Documents

  • Doc 19: Importer Acceptance Field (Movement Instructions) - OECD decision text and movement/operation code instructions.
  • US EPA: Import-side Shipment Controls - International hazardous waste shipment control overview.

Block 18: Receipt at Facility

Block 18 – Quick Reference

Receipt at Facility

Confirms receiving facility physically received the declared shipment.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B
Field Type
Facility gate receipt
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 18 Captures

Block 18 is the facility intake checkpoint for quantity/condition reconciliation.

It supports traceability between transport completion and treatment start.

How to Complete Block 18

1
Record facility receipt date and receiving signatory.
2
Verify received quantity/condition against movement details.
3
Document any variance with evidence.
4
Escalate unresolved discrepancies immediately.
⚠️
Receipt Gaps Delay Closure

Missing or unclear receipt evidence can stall compliance closeout and reconciliation.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
No signed intake evidence.
Correct
Capture signed receipt at gate intake.
Wrong
Unexplained quantity variance.
Correct
Document cause and corrective action.
Wrong
Condition issues not recorded.
Correct
Log condition exceptions at receipt.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can receipt be issued with remarks?▼

Yes, conditional receipt is acceptable with clear notes.

Should photos be attached?▼

Photos are useful for discrepancy evidence.

Who keeps receipt archive?▼

Facility and exporter should both retain copies.

Block 19: Certification of Disposal/Recovery

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 19

Block 19 – Quick Reference

Certification of Disposal/Recovery

Provides final certified proof that approved treatment operation was completed.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B and completion obligations
Field Type
Final completion certification
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 19 Captures

Block 19 closes the movement lifecycle and confirms treatment completion under approved terms.

This certification is often required before financial guarantee release.

How to Complete Block 19

1
Obtain authorized facility certification after treatment completion.
2
Record completion date and confirmed operation details.
3
Issue certification to required parties and authorities on time.
4
Retain auditable completion evidence for compliance records.
⚠️
No Block 19 = Movement Not Legally Closed

Missing final certification can keep guarantees locked and trigger enforcement concerns.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Certification not returned to exporter/authorities.
Correct
Distribute final certification within required timeline.
Wrong
Certified operation differs from approved code.
Correct
Certify only actual approved operation completed.
Wrong
Late issuance without explanation.
Correct
Document timeline and corrective actions where delayed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why is Block 19 financially important?▼

It is commonly required before guarantee/bond release.

Who signs Block 19?▼

Authorized facility representative after completion.

What if completion is partial?▼

Document status clearly and follow authority instructions before final closure.

Supporting Documents

  • Doc 19: Certification of Disposal/Recovery Instructions - OECD decision text and movement/operation code instructions.

item.title: Basel Compliance Checklist
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
[su_note note_color="#e8f4fd"] Doc #27: Basel Compliance Checklist
Use this checklist to verify your Basel notification pack is complete, internally consistent, and defensible under Environmentally Sound Management (ESM). Most delays happen when the receiving facility permit scope doesn’t match the intended operation, the wrong site address is used, or annexes don’t align with the form entries. [/su_note]

← Back to Basel Knowledge Hub

What This Checklist Verifies

  • Completeness: required parties, signatures, annexes, and supporting evidence are present.
  • Consistency: Basel codes, waste description, quantities, routing, and contacts match across the form and annexes.
  • Facility readiness (ESM): the receiving facility authorization, operational site address, and emergency preparedness are credible for the intended operation.
  • Shipment readiness: Movement Document details will mirror the approved Notification.

Pre-Submission Checklist (Fast Audit)

1) Parties & Contacts

  • Exporter/Notifier legal name + address match registration and contract documents.
  • Importer/Consignee details match the receiving facility documentation.
  • Competent authorities correctly identified for export/import (and transit if applicable).

2) Waste Identification

  • Waste description is specific (composition, form, key hazards) — not generic “scrap”.
  • Basel codes and any national codes are consistent across form + annexes.
  • Quantities/units match the contract and intended shipment schedule.

3) Operation & Facility Permit Match (Most Common Failure Point)

  • Intended operation (recovery/disposal) is clearly stated and consistent throughout.
  • Receiving facility permit/license is current and legible (valid dates cover shipment window).
  • Permit scope explicitly covers the intended operation and the waste type.
  • Operational site address (where treatment occurs) matches Block 7 + permit docs (not head office).

4) Contract, Insurance & Coverage

  • Contract aligns with waste description, quantities, and responsibilities (including residues/returns if applicable).
  • Insurance/financial coverage evidence is current and linked to the shipment scope.

5) Movement Document Readiness (Before Shipment)

  • Movement Document will mirror the approved Notification (waste description, quantities, routing, parties).
  • Emergency contacts + supporting transport documents will be with the shipment.
[su_divider top="no"] [su_note note_color="#fff3cd"] Common Failure Points: Facility permit mismatch (operation not covered), wrong address (registered office vs operational site), missing annexes, or inconsistencies between Notification and Movement Document (waste description, quantity, routing, or parties). [/su_note]

Related Documents

  • Doc #10: Emergency Response Plan ✅ - Site-specific emergency preparedness evidence supporting ESM.
  • Transport Documentation ✅ - Hazard communication and transit controls that support shipment readiness.
  • Basel Form Guide ✅ - Return to the form block-by-block guidance.

item.title: Emergency Response Plan
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
[su_note note_color="#e8f4fd"] The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is a core supporting document used to demonstrate that the receiving facility identified in Block 7 can manage incidents safely and maintain environmentally sound management (ESM). Competent authorities often expect an ERP (or equivalent site-specific emergency procedures) where the waste stream presents credible risks (e.g., flammable solvents, corrosives, batteries, ULABs, reactive chemicals). A generic corporate HSE manual is rarely sufficient — the plan must be site-specific and aligned to the facility’s permitted operations. [/su_note]

← Back to Knowledge Hub

What This Document Covers

This ERP is the facility’s operational playbook for managing emergencies that could occur during receipt, storage, handling, and processing of hazardous waste. It supports the facility’s claim of capability under Block 7 and helps demonstrate that the site can respond to incidents without creating additional cross-border environmental harm.

When Authorities Expect It

  • Higher-risk waste streams: flammable liquids, corrosives, toxics, reactive waste, batteries, ULABs, e-waste, or mixed hazardous residues.
  • Thermal or chemical treatment: incineration (D10), physico-chemical treatment (D9), metal recovery (R4), battery recycling operations, or any process involving heat/acid/alkali.
  • Facilities with complex logistics: multiple storage areas, intermediate handling steps, subcontracted operations, or shared industrial sites.
  • Where the permit requires it: many national environmental permits include emergency preparedness obligations and reporting timelines.

Required Sections

  • Facility Identification: legal entity, site address (operational location), 24/7 emergency contact details, and after-hours escalation chain.
  • Site Layout & Control Points: site map showing storage zones, processing areas, drainage controls, bunding, spill kits, extinguishers, isolation valves, and muster points.
  • Credible Emergency Scenarios: spill/leak, fire/explosion, gas release, incompatible mixing, runaway battery event, container rupture, vehicle incident, and severe weather/flooding impacts where relevant.
  • Immediate Response Procedures: isolate area, stop source, contain/collect, prevent discharge to drains, decontamination steps, and safe temporary storage of cleanup residues.
  • PPE & Equipment: minimum PPE by scenario, location of equipment, maintenance/inspection schedule, and responsible persons.
  • Notifications & Reporting: who must be notified (internal + external), timelines, incident log requirements, and corrective/preventive actions (CAPA).
  • Training & Drills: induction training, refresher training frequency, drill schedule, and records retention.
  • Interface With Transport: receiving procedures for damaged loads, emergency handover, and how transport documents (SDS / emergency instructions) are used on arrival.

Common Gaps That Trigger Questions

  • Not site-specific: a corporate policy document without site maps, equipment locations, or scenario procedures.
  • No linkage to waste hazards: ERP does not address the actual chemicals/materials listed in the notification (e.g., acids for ULABs, thermal risk for lithium batteries).
  • Missing 24/7 contacts: only business-hour phone numbers provided, with no escalation path.
  • Unclear containment controls: no detail on bunding, drainage isolation, or how spills are prevented from reaching soil/water.
  • No proof of readiness: absent drill records, equipment inspections, or training evidence.

How To Use It In a Basel Notification Pack

Attach the facility ERP (or the emergency preparedness section of the facility’s permit package) as a supporting document referenced in your submission. Ensure the ERP aligns to the facility named in Block 7 and the operation identified in Block 10. Where the ERP is lengthy, include a one-page ERP summary highlighting the emergency contacts, response capabilities, and containment controls.

Real-World Example

A lead-acid battery recycler receiving ULABs maintains a site-specific ERP that includes acid spill neutralization procedures, lead exposure controls, containment to prevent discharge to drains, and a 24/7 emergency escalation chain. The ERP references equipment locations (spill kits, neutralizing agents, bunded areas) and includes drill records and inspection logs.

Related Documents

  • Transport Documentation ✅ - Emergency instructions, hazard communication, and transport controls that interface with facility receiving procedures.
  • Basel Compliance Checklist ✅ - A consolidated checklist to verify your notification pack is complete and internally consistent.
[su_divider top="no"] [su_note note_color="#fff3cd"] Common Error: Uploading a generic “Health & Safety Policy” and calling it an emergency plan. Authorities (and auditors) look for site-specific procedures: scenario response steps, site map, equipment locations, 24/7 contacts, containment controls, and evidence of training/drills. If the facility operates multiple sites, the ERP must match the exact operational site address identified in Block 7. [/su_note] [su_note note_color="#d4edda"] Compliance Tip: For ULAB and e-waste shipments, validate that the ERP specifically covers acid spills, fire/thermal events, and contaminated cleanup residues. Confirm the facility has practical controls (bunding/drain isolation, neutralization agents, spill kits) and that emergency contacts are reachable 24/7. If the receiving facility uses subcontractors (e.g., off-site treatment), document the emergency interface and responsibilities clearly. [/su_note] [su_divider top="no"] [su_button url="/data-library/" style="flat" background="#1a3a5c" color="#ffffff"]Back to Knowledge Hub[/su_button]

[su_note note_color="#e8f4fd"] Doc #28: Correspondence Record Log
Use this log to track every interaction with the Competent Authority of Import (and any transit authorities where applicable). It creates an audit-ready timeline from notification submission to acknowledgement, requests for correction, final consent/conditions, shipment scheduling, and closure confirmations. [/su_note]

← Back to Basel Knowledge Hub

What This Log Captures

  • Authority communications: emails, letters, calls, meetings, portal submissions, and acknowledgements.
  • Requests & actions: clarification requests, missing annexes, corrections, and resubmissions.
  • Deadlines: response due dates, consent expiry, shipment windows, and conditions.
  • Evidence trail: file names/links to letters, permits, annexes, and updated forms.

Required Fields

  • Date/Time (and time zone if cross-border)
  • Authority (Import / Transit / Export)
  • Contact Person + Office
  • Channel (Email / Letter / Call / Portal)
  • Subject / Reference # (notification #, tracking #, case ID)
  • Summary of Message (what was requested/confirmed)
  • Action Owner + Due Date
  • Status / Outcome (Pending / Submitted / Accepted / Closed)
  • Attachment Link(s) (where evidence is stored)

Log Template (Copy This Table)

During authority review, it becomes difficult to prove when a request was received, what was submitted in response, and which version of an annex or form was provided. A structured log prevents missed deadlines and reduces resubmission cycles. Package/handling controls

Apply compliant labels before handoff.

Can packaging change during movement?▼

item.title: Block 11: Disposal/Recovery Operation
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Block 11: Disposal/Recovery Operation

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 11

Block 11 – Quick Reference

Disposal/Recovery Operation

Confirms the approved operation code and technology to be applied to the waste at the receiving facility.

Basel Basis
Annex IV-A (Disposal) / IV-B (Recovery) and ESM principles
Field Type
Operation code (R/D) and technology
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 11 Captures

Block 11 records the specific legal operation — not just the facility, but exactly what will be done to the waste once it arrives. Every Basel movement must declare either a D-code (disposal) or an R-code (recovery) drawn from the standardized lists in Annex IV of the Basel Convention.

The declared operation code must:

  • Match the code authorized in the original notification
  • Align with the receiving facility's permit scope (Block 10)
  • Correspond to the actual technology employed at that facility

If Block 10 tells authorities where the waste is going, Block 11 tells them what happens to it — and competent authorities use these two blocks together to assess the legality and environmental soundness of the movement.

R-Codes: Recovery Operations

Code Operation
R1Use as fuel or other energy generation
R2Solvent reclamation/regeneration
R3Recycling/reclamation of organic substances (non-solvent)
R4Recycling/reclamation of metals and metal compounds
R5Recycling/reclamation of other inorganic materials
R6Regeneration of acids or bases
R7Recovery of components for pollution abatement
R8Recovery of components from catalysts
R9Used oil re-refining or other reuses of previously used oil
R10Land treatment for agricultural or ecological benefit
R11Uses of residual materials from R1–R10
R12Exchange of wastes for submission to R1–R11
R13Accumulation of material intended for any operation in this list
💡
ULAB / Battery Recycling note

Lead-acid battery recycling typically uses R4 (metals and metal compounds). Confirm against your facility authorization before declaring.

D-Codes: Disposal Operations

Code Operation
D1Deposit into or onto land (landfill)
D2Land treatment (biodegradation)
D3Deep injection
D4Surface impoundment
D5Specially engineered landfill
D6Release into water body (except seas/oceans)
D7Release into seas/oceans
D8Biological treatment not elsewhere specified
D9Physico-chemical treatment not elsewhere specified
D10Incineration on land
D11Incineration at sea
D12Permanent storage
D13Blending or mixing prior to another D operation
D14Repackaging prior to another D operation
D15Storage pending any D operation

How to Complete Block 11

1
Determine whether the movement is for disposal or recovery. This must match the notification.
2
Select the single most accurate R-code or D-code from the tables above.
3
State the technology employed at the facility (e.g., "pyrometallurgical smelting," "hydrometallurgical leaching," "mechanical shredding and separation").
4
Cross-reference against the facility's current permit (Block 10) to confirm the declared operation is within authorized scope.
⚠️
R12/R13 and D13–D15 Interim Operations

If the declared operation is R12, R13, D13, D14, or D15, you must attach an annex identifying the subsequent facility where the final R1–R11 or D1–D12 operation will be completed. Block 11 alone is not sufficient for interim operations.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Using R4 when facility is only authorized for R13
Correct
Declare the actual authorized operation; attach annex for subsequent R4 facility
Wrong
Changing the operation code on the movement document without authority approval
Correct
Obtain formal variation from competent authority before any code change
Wrong
Listing a technology that does not match the declared R/D code
Correct
Technology description must logically correspond to the declared code
Wrong
Leaving the technology field blank
Correct
Always specify technology — it is required for competent authority assessment

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I change the operation code after the notification is approved?▼

No. The code on the movement document must match the approved notification. Any change requires a formal variation through the competent authority before the shipment departs.

Can R and D codes be used interchangeably?▼

No. Recovery (R) and disposal (D) are legally distinct categories under the Basel Convention. Using the wrong category can invalidate consent and expose the exporter to enforcement action.

What if my waste goes through an interim operation before final recovery?▼

Declare the interim operation (R12 or R13) in Block 11, and attach an annex identifying the subsequent facility and the final operation (R1–R11) where the actual recovery takes place.

Is Block 11 the same in the notification and movement document?▼

The notification Block 11 has three sub-fields: D/R code, technology employed, and reason for export. The movement document Block 11 is simplified to D/R code only. Do not deviate from the approved notification.

Supporting Documents

  • Doc 5: Classification Guide (R/D Codes) — R and D code definitions per Basel Annex IV.
  • Doc 16: Process Flow Diagram — Technology description and operation flow for facility authorization.
  • Doc 19: Movement Form Instructions (Block 11) — Official Basel completion instructions for operation fields.
💡
DexMetal Expert Tip

Always validate Block 11 against the facility's current permit and the approved notification before dispatch. A mismatch between the movement document and the notification is one of the most common grounds for shipment rejection at the border.

item.title: Block 13: Physical Characteristics
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
custom

html

Block 13: Physical Characteristics

← Basel Knowledge Hub / Basel Movement Guide / Block 13

Block 13 – Quick Reference

Physical Characteristics

Identifies the physical state of the waste at normal temperature and pressure using standardized codes.

Basel Basis
Annex V-B Block 13
Field Type
Physical state code(s)
Required For
All Basel movements

What Block 13 Captures

Block 13 declares the physical state of the waste under normal temperature and pressure conditions. It uses the same standardized code list as the notification document — the movement document must carry a consistent declaration. Competent authorities and emergency responders use this block during transit to understand the physical form of the material being carried.

For wastes with more than one physical state — such as lead-acid batteries, which have a solid casing and plates combined with a liquid electrolyte — all applicable codes must be declared. Declaring only one code when more apply is a common error that creates a misleading hazard profile for transport authorities.

Physical Characteristics Codes

1
Powdery / Powder — Fine solid particulate material.
2
Solid — Material with a defined shape and volume that does not flow under gravity.
3
Viscous / Paste — Semi-solid material that flows slowly under pressure.
4
Sludgy — A mixture of liquid and solid material with a semi-fluid consistency.
5
Liquid — Material that flows freely under gravity at normal temperature and pressure.
6
Gaseous — Material in gas phase at normal temperature and pressure.
7
Other — Any physical state not covered by codes 1–6. Must be described in full — do not select Other without specifying the state.
⚠️
Must Match the Approved Notification

The physical characteristics declared on the movement document must be consistent with what was declared on the notification. A discrepancy between the two documents will draw authority queries and can delay the shipment at the border.

How To Complete Block 13

  1. Identify the physical form of the waste. Choose from the Basel Convention Annex III categories: solid, liquid, sludge, gas, or other. Select the category that best describes the waste as it will be packaged for shipment.
  2. Describe the physical state at the time of shipment. Use clear, objective language — e.g., "crushed and baled", "shredded", "intact units", "granulated". Avoid vague terms like "mixed" without further specification.
  3. Match the description to your notification. The physical characteristics recorded on the movement document must be consistent with the description submitted in the original notification. Do not upgrade or downgrade the physical state without notifying the competent authorities.
  4. Confirm packaging compatibility. The physical form must align with the packaging type declared elsewhere in the document. Authorities will cross-check Block 13 against packaging declarations and transport documents.

Common Errors – Correct Approach

Wrong
Selecting only code 2 (Solid) for ULABs
Correct
Select both code 2 (Solid) and code 5 (Liquid) — ULABs contain solid plates and liquid sulfuric acid electrolyte
Wrong
Selecting code 7 (Other) without describing the physical state
Correct
Always provide a full description when selecting Other — never leave it unspecified
Wrong
Block 13 on the movement document differs from Block 13 on the approved notification
Correct
Both documents must carry identical physical characteristics codes — check consistency before dispatch
Wrong
No code selected — Block 13 left blank
Correct
At least one code must be declared — Block 13 is mandatory on every movement document

Frequently Asked Questions

Can more than one code be selected?▼

Yes. Where the waste has more than one physical state — as is the case with lead-acid batteries — all applicable codes should be declared. For ULABs, codes 2 (Solid) and 5 (Liquid) both apply.

Does Block 13 on the movement document need to match the notification exactly?▼

Yes. The movement document must be consistent with the approved notification. Any discrepancy in physical characteristics between the two documents can trigger authority queries at the border and delay the shipment.

What codes apply to sealed (VRLA/AGM) batteries that are non-spillable?▼

Sealed VRLA and AGM batteries still contain electrolyte in absorbed or gel form. Code 2 (Solid) applies to the casing and plates. Whether code 5 (Liquid) or code 3 (Viscous/Paste) applies to the electrolyte depends on the specific battery type — confirm with the battery manufacturer's technical data sheet and declare consistently with the approved notification.

Supporting Documents

  • vCOP8 Official Movement Document — Annex V-B Block 13 — Official Basel source for the physical characteristics code list and completion instructions.
💡
DexMetal Expert Tip

For ULAB exports, the correct Block 13 entry is codes 2 and 5 — Solid and Liquid. This applies to both flooded and sealed battery types. Declare it the same way on every movement document under a general notification to maintain consistency with the approved notification and avoid any document-to-document discrepancies that could attract scrutiny.

Basel Convention Reference

⚡ Notification Document — Quick View

All 21 blocks at a glance. Click any block for full guidance.

How to use this page: Scan all 21 blocks before starting your notification. Click any block title for complete field-level guidance, common errors, and country-specific requirements.

Blocks 1–10: Parties & Logistics

Block What it covers Completed by
Block 1: Exporter-Notifier Exporter's registration details, address, contact, and national ID number Exporter
Block 2: Importer-Consignee Importer's registration details, address, and contact information Exporter
Block 3: Notification Number & Shipment Type Unique tracking number assigned by competent authority; single or general notification type Competent Authority
Block 4: Total Number of Shipments Planned number of individual shipments under this notification Exporter
Block 5: Total Intended Quantity Total weight or volume of waste across all shipments; unit of measurement required Exporter
Block 6: Intended Period of Shipment(s) Start and end dates for all planned shipments under this notification Exporter
Block 7: Packaging Type(s) & Special Handling Packaging codes (UN type), labelling, and any special handling requirements Exporter
Block 8: Intended Carrier(s) All transport companies handling the waste; name, address, licence number, transport mode Exporter
Block 9: Waste Generator-Producer Original producer of the waste; name, address, site of generation Exporter
Block 10: Disposal/Recovery Facility Receiving facility details; name, address, permit number, operation type Exporter

Blocks 11–21: Technical & Administrative

Block What it covers Completed by
Block 11: Disposal/Recovery Operation Basel Annex III/IV operation code (e.g. R4 for metal recovery) Exporter
Block 12: Designation & Composition of Waste Technical description of waste; physical state, chemical composition, major contaminants Exporter
Block 13: Physical Characteristics Physical form: solid, liquid, sludge, powder, other Exporter
Block 14: Waste Identification Codes Basel Annex VIII/IX codes, OECD codes, national codes — all applicable must be listed Exporter
Block 15: Countries/States & Border Crossings All countries of export, transit, and import; entry/exit border crossing points Exporter
Block 16: Customs Offices (EU Only) EU customs office codes for entry and exit points — EU Member State shipments only Exporter
Block 17: Exporter & Generator Declaration Signed declaration that all information is accurate and complete; exporter signature and date Exporter
Block 18: Number of Annexes Attached Count of all supporting documents attached to the notification Exporter
Block 19: Competent Authority Acknowledgement Receipt confirmation from exporting country's competent authority; date stamped Competent Authority
Block 20: Competent Authority Consent/Objection Written consent, conditional consent, or objection from all relevant competent authorities Competent Authority
Block 21: Specific Conditions or Objection Reasons Any conditions attached to consent or stated grounds for objection Competent Authority

⚡ Common Rejection Triggers

Blocks 12, 14, and 15 account for the majority of notification rejections. Waste composition, classification codes, and country routing errors are the top three failure points. Double-check these before submission.

item.title: Basel Movement Document — Quick View Checklist
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Basel Convention Reference

⚡ Movement Document — Quick View

All movement document blocks at a glance. Click any block for full guidance.

Important: The movement document travels with the waste shipment. It must be completed in sequence — exporter fields before departure, carrier fields during transit, facility fields on arrival. Do not complete all fields in advance.

Pre-Shipment Blocks (Completed Before Departure)

Block What it covers Completed by
Block 1: Notification Number Must match the approved notification number exactly Exporter
Block 2: Serial Number Sequential shipment number (e.g. 1 of 5) under this notification Exporter
Block 3: Exporter-Notifier Exporter details — must match Block 1 of the approved notification Exporter
Block 4: Importer-Consignee Importer details — must match Block 2 of the approved notification Exporter
Block 5: Actual Quantity Actual weight/volume of this specific shipment (not total notification quantity) Exporter
Block 6: Actual Date of Shipment Date waste leaves the exporter's facility — completed on departure day Exporter
Block 7: Packaging Actual packaging used; UN type codes and special handling markings Exporter
Block 8: Special Handling Instructions for emergency situations during transport Exporter
Block 9: Waste Identification Basel/OECD classification codes for the waste in this shipment Exporter

In-Transit & Arrival Blocks

Block What it covers Completed by
Block 10: Disposal/Recovery Facility Receiving facility confirmation details Exporter
Block 11: Disposal/Recovery Operation Actual operation code to be performed at the receiving facility Exporter
Block 12: Waste Designation Composition confirmation of waste in this shipment Exporter
Block 13: Carrier Information Actual carrier details; signature and date on taking custody of waste Carrier
Block 14: Waste Identification (Movement) Re-confirmation of waste codes at point of collection Carrier
Block 15: Exporter Declaration Exporter's signed declaration that shipment matches notification terms Exporter
Block 16: Customs Offices Actual customs offices used at border crossings (EU shipments) Carrier
Block 17: Importer Acceptance Importer's signed confirmation of receipt; date and quantity received Importer
Block 18: Facility Receipt Facility operator's signed confirmation of receipt and intended operation Facility
Block 19: Disposal/Recovery Certification Facility's final certification that disposal/recovery was completed as declared Facility

⚡ Movement Document Rule

Block 19 (Disposal Certification) must be returned to the exporting country's competent authority within 180 days of shipment. Missing this deadline is a Basel Convention violation.

item.title: Basel Waste Code Quick Lookup Table
item.dc:creator: rdavid@gvoltt.com
item.content:encoded:
Basel Convention Reference

⚡ Basel Waste Code — Quick Lookup

Annex VIII (A-codes), Annex IX (B-codes), and OECD codes for e-waste and battery waste streams.

How to use this table: Find your waste stream in the Description column. Use the corresponding code in Block 14 of your notification form and Block 9 of your movement document. Always list all applicable codes.

Annex VIII — Hazardous Waste (A-Codes)

These wastes are presumed hazardous under Basel. Require full prior informed consent from all competent authorities.

Code Description Common E-Waste Examples
A1010 Metal wastes and waste consisting of alloys of antimony, arsenic, beryllium, cadmium, lead, mercury, selenium, tellurium, thallium CRT screens, NiCd batteries
A1180 Waste electrical and electronic assemblies or scrap containing components such as accumulators, mercury-switches, glass from cathode-ray tubes Mixed e-waste, CRT monitors, circuit boards with hazardous components
A1181 Waste electrical and electronic assemblies or scrap not listed under A1180, containing components such as accumulators, printed circuit boards Laptops, phones, TVs — primary e-waste export code
A1020 Waste having as constituents lead and lead compounds Lead-acid batteries (ULABs), CRT glass
A1030 Waste having as constituents mercury compounds LCD backlights (CCFL), fluorescent lamps
A1160 Waste lead-acid batteries, whole or crushed ULABs — dedicated ULAB export code

Annex IX — Non-Hazardous Waste (B-Codes)

These wastes are presumed non-hazardous under Basel but may still require notification under national law or OECD rules.

Code Description Common E-Waste Examples
B1010 Metal and metal-alloy wastes in metallic, non-dispersible form Clean copper, aluminium, steel scrap from e-waste processing
B1110 Electrical and electronic assemblies — only those free of components such as accumulators, mercury-switches, CRT glass, asbestos Tested/working electronics for reuse, cleaned circuit boards
B3010 Solid plastic waste of non-halogenated polymers ABS, polypropylene casings from sorted e-waste
Y49 Waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) — non-hazardous Used alongside B1110 for non-hazardous e-waste streams

OECD Recovery Operation Codes

Required in Block 11 (notification) and Block 11 (movement document) for all OECD member state shipments.

Code Operation E-Waste Application
R4 Recycling/reclamation of metals and metal compounds Primary code for ULAB and metal e-waste recycling
R3 Recycling/reclamation of organic substances not used as solvents Plastic recovery from e-waste processing
R5 Recycling/reclamation of other inorganic materials Glass, ceramic components from e-waste
R12 Exchange of wastes for submission to any of operations numbered R1–R11 Pre-processing / sorting facilities before final recovery
D15 Storage pending any of operations D1–D14 (excluding temporary storage) Bonded warehouse storage before disposal

⚠️ Code Selection Warning

Using a B-code (non-hazardous) for waste that contains hazardous components is a Basel violation. When in doubt, use the A-code. Competent authorities can downgrade; they cannot upgrade after consent is granted.
